supporting_pages.title: Migrate from DynamoDB to Bigtable \_|\_ Google Cloud Documentation
evidence_snippets: Geographic replication Replication is used to support customer requirements for the following: High availability for business continuity in the event of a zonal or regional failure.
Replication: A way to increase the availability and durability of your data by automatically propagating data changes across multiple regions or multiple zones within the same region.
Global tables: A way to increase availability and durability of your data by automatically propagating data changes across multiple regions.

supporting_pages.title: Schema design best practices \_|\_ Bigtable \_|\_ Google Cloud Documentation
evidence_snippets: For example, if your row key includes a continent, country, and city, you can create row keys that look like the following so that they automatically sort first by values with lower cardinality: asia#india#bangalore asia#india#mumbai asia#japan#osaka asia#japan#sapporo southamerica#bolivia#cochabamba southamerica#bolivia#lapaz southamerica#chile#santiago southamerica#chile#temuco Note: In production, use identifiers that take up less storage, such as AS for Asia or 591 for Bolivia.
Each cell adds some overhead to the amount of data that's stored in your table and sent over the network.
